proposed_additions.question: A Red Exile’s pawn is at a faceup site garrisoned by purple warbands, while red warbands occupy a different faceup site without their pawn. Which site and its denizen cards does Red rule? Does moving the pawn by itself change rule, and can red and purple site warbands coexist to share rule of one site?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Red rules the faceup site containing their red warbands and the cards at that site, even though their pawn is elsewhere. Red does not rule the purple-garrisoned site merely because their pawn is there. A player also rules their own advisers. Moving a pawn by itself does not move the site warbands or change this basis of rule. A site can hold warbands of only one color at a time; different colors do not share a site by coexisting there. Imperial players share rule of purple-garrisoned sites under the Empire exception, rather than by placing different colors together.
material_facts: Rule of a faceup site depends on a player’s warbands there, not pawn presence.
Rule extends to cards at ruled sites and to the player’s own advisers.
A site holds warbands of only one color; Imperial shared rule is the purple-warband exception.
source_references: Law 10, Rule, corrected by errata to faceup sites
Playbook p8, Ruling Sites on the Map
Playbook p18: pawns do not matter for rule
proposed_additions.novelty: Positive rule criterion and its pawn/garrison boundary; one-color site constraint. Q066 only tests faceup eligibility/ruins, Q091 bandit victory exclusion, and Q032 presupposes that a site is ruled. No credit for repeated faceup, bandit, or Imperial facts.

proposed_additions.question: A power tells you to reveal a facedown card, without telling you to play it. Who sees its front? Is this the same instruction as peeking, and does revealing alone award favor for site play or trigger a When Played power?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Reveal means show the card’s front to everyone. Peek means the prompted player looks at its front. Revealing alone is not an instruction to Play: it does not itself put a card at a site, in advisers, or in a personal bank. Therefore the reveal alone does not grant the favor for playing to a site or trigger a When Played power. If the effect separately instructs you to play the card, follow that instruction and the ordinary play restrictions and triggers.
material_facts: Reveal shows the front to everyone; Peek is looking at the front.
A reveal-only instruction is distinct from Play and does not itself trigger play rewards or When Played powers.
source_references: Law 5.1.4.I gain for playing to site
proposed_additions.novelty: Operational Reveal definition and reveal-only versus play outcome. Q010 concerns actually playing an adviser faceup; Q033 concerns permitted peeks; Q089 distinguishes Move/Swap from Play but does not test Reveal. This is not another adviser-reveal example.

proposed_additions.question: While resolving a power, an instruction says to do something “after” a specified event. May you postpone that instruction until after an intervening step of the same action? What exact timing does “after” prescribe?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: No. After means immediately following: nothing happens between the specified event and the prompted instruction. It does not provide a discretionary later window within the action. Follow any explicit text governing the actual effect; this definition does not invent a priority rule for simultaneous effects.
material_facts: After means immediately following, with nothing happening between.
The instruction cannot simply be deferred to a later step of the same action.
proposed_additions.novelty: Generic immediate timing word. Q029 tests the specific order of When Played prerequisites; Q068 tests finishing one action before starting another. Neither states the no-intervening-step meaning of After within an action.

proposed_additions.question: Unless an effect specifies different locations, where do favor/secrets, an adviser card, and a relic move when you Take them? How does Give reverse the direction? If a power simply tells you to Burn a favor or secret, can you choose a token on a banner or card instead of your board, and where does it go?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Take moves the prompted favor or secrets from the prompted player’s board to your board, a card from their advisers to your advisers, or a relic from their personal bank—or the prompted site or draw source—to your personal bank. Give is the reverse direction of Take. Burn normally moves the prompted favor or secret from your own board to the shared bank; another location is used only if the effect prompts it. A plain Burn instruction does not let you substitute a token from a banner or card. Follow the actual prompt and applicable placement/restriction rules.
material_facts: Take has defined source and destination locations for player resources, advisers and relics.
Burn defaults to the acting player’s board and the shared bank; other source locations require a prompt.
proposed_additions.novelty: Default transfer sources/destinations and board-only default for Burn. Q042 establishes that Give and Take restrictions differ, not these locations; named Recover, Campaign, discard, and Citizenship transfers do not test the general defaults. No credit for repeating those named transfers.

proposed_additions.question: A power permits an Exchange with a prompted player, without adding a must instruction or a binding agreement. What permission does Exchange give each player? Does the word alone require both players to transfer equal amounts in a simultaneous swap?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Exchange means you may Give to the prompted player and vice versa: each player has the stated permission to Give to the other. The word by itself does not impose a compulsory, equal-amount, simultaneous exchange. The actual power still controls which pieces and amounts are permitted, and any explicit binding promise or other instruction must be followed. Swap is a different instruction that moves the two prompted pieces to each other’s locations.
material_facts: Exchange grants optional permission to Give in both directions between the prompted players.
Equality, compulsory reciprocal transfer and simultaneity are not extra requirements supplied by the word alone; the actual prompt controls.
source_references: Law 7.6.3 and 9.6 for the separate binding-promise rule
proposed_additions.novelty: Affirmative optional bilateral Exchange permission. Q043 and Q064 test binding negotiation exceptions and Tribunal’s allowed assets/future actions; they do not state this generic permission. No additional credit for repeated binding or Swap facts.

versioned_key_clarifications.old_expected_answer: Anyone even Imperials. Burn one secret,take one relic/banner from player whose pawn at own site; two own faceup advisers each match suit of any enemy adviser,can both match same adviser. Does not replace revealed true Vision; banner seizure applies; Conspiracy goes box even no theft.
versioned_key_clarifications.proposed_expected_answer: Anyone, even Imperials. Burn one secret to take one relic or banner from any player whose pawn is at your site. Two of your own faceup advisers must each match the suit of at least one of that target player’s advisers; both may match the same adviser. The target need not be an enemy. Playing Conspiracy does not replace a revealed true Vision; banner seizure applies; Conspiracy goes to the box even if no theft is made.
versioned_key_clarifications.reason: Remove enemy-only ambiguity while retaining the already-correct any co-located player target rule. Historical inputs remain intact.

coverage_assessment.zero_pass_conclusion: The recorded zero passes do not survive this fresh challenge. Existing maps attach After/Reveal/Rule/Exchange/transfer definitions to questions that test related but different operations. Add and source-review the genuine missing rules, then restart the consecutive zero-addition sweeps.

procedural_passage_review.assessment: Both first packet recipe and later saved-world setup, markers, banks, garrisons, initial advisers/Visions, relic ordering/randomization and initial Archive preparation accounted for. Unrebuilt-deck setup uses the same recipe already tested by Q020, not a novel additional procedure.
All Oaths/Visions, successions, ties/round-eight priority, title flipping, banner/Wake sequence, opportunity income, Act completion and Rest/saving branches accounted for.

Search costs/sources/mandatory stopping and draw count, discard and play destinations, advisers/Visions/Conspiracy, Muster, both Trade branches and all Recover/banner conditions accounted for. Q031 needs target-player wording clarification, not a new scenario question.

procedural_passage_review.assessment: Defender/target eligibility, both side outcomes, attack/defense force, skulls, sacrifice, bandits, Imperial allies/status/payments/order, mandatory modifiers, defeat/victory effects and outcome-independent cleanup accounted for.

Travel matrix/reveal and named exceptions, adviser play, peeks, movement permissions, offer/acceptance, conversion shortages and both exile procedures accounted for. Positive rule criterion is a distinct uncovered prerequisite, A01.
